data_questions.question: Does the customer-data bucket (aws_s3_bucket.customer_data) hold personal data (names, emails, addresses, account or ID numbers)?
data_questions.why: Personal data raises the stakes of every path to it, and brings legal duties.

data_questions.question: Does the customer-data bucket (aws_s3_bucket.customer_data) hold passwords, keys or tokens?
data_questions.why: Stored credentials turn one leak into many.

questions.question: Does the app server (aws_instance.app) check every request's input (type, length, format) before using it?
questions.why: Unchecked input is how injection attacks start.

questions.question: Does the web load balancer (aws_lb.web) check every request's input (type, length, format) before using it? (For a load balancer: is a WAF rule doing this in front of the app?)
questions.why: Unchecked input is how injection attacks start.

questions.question: Does the app server (aws_instance.app) clean or escape input before it reaches a database, a shell or a template?
questions.why: Input that reaches a query or a command unescaped can run as code.

questions.question: Does the app server (aws_instance.app) encode what it sends back (HTML/JSON escaping), so user data can't become code in a browser?
questions.why: Unencoded output is how cross-site scripting happens.

questions.question: Does the web load balancer (aws_lb.web) clean or escape input before it reaches a database, a shell or a template? (For a load balancer: is a WAF rule doing this in front of the app?)
questions.why: Input that reaches a query or a command unescaped can run as code.

questions.question: Does the web load balancer (aws_lb.web) encode what it sends back (HTML/JSON escaping), so user data can't become code in a browser? (For a load balancer: is a WAF rule doing this in front of the app?)
questions.why: Unencoded output is how cross-site scripting happens.

questions.question: Does the app server (aws_instance.app) check what the caller is allowed to do before every action?
questions.why: Missing checks let one user read or change another user's data.

questions.question: Are the session IDs issued by the app server (aws_instance.app) long, random and replaced at login?
questions.why: Guessable or fixed session IDs let attackers take over sessions.

questions.question: Does the web load balancer (aws_lb.web) check what the caller is allowed to do before every action?
questions.why: Missing checks let one user read or change another user's data.

questions.question: Is the web load balancer (aws_lb.web) hardened: unused services off, patched, running as a least-privilege user?
questions.why: Every extra service or privilege is extra attack surface.

questions.question: Are the session IDs issued by the web load balancer (aws_lb.web) long, random and replaced at login?
questions.why: Guessable or fixed session IDs let attackers take over sessions.

questions.question: Does the app server (aws_instance.app) require callers to prove who they are (login, token, mTLS)?
questions.why: Anonymous callers can use anything that doesn't ask.

questions.question: After authentication, does the app server (aws_instance.app) check that this caller may do this specific thing?
questions.why: Authenticated is not the same as allowed.

questions.question: Is the app server (aws_instance.app) hardened: unused services off, patched, running as a least-privilege user?
questions.why: Every extra service or privilege is extra attack surface.

questions.question: Does the app server (aws_instance.app) reject malformed HTTP headers?
questions.why: Malformed headers enable request smuggling.

questions.question: Does the web load balancer (aws_lb.web) require callers to prove who they are (login, token, mTLS)?
questions.why: Anonymous callers can use anything that doesn't ask.

questions.question: After authentication, does the web load balancer (aws_lb.web) check that this caller may do this specific thing?
questions.why: Authenticated is not the same as allowed.

questions.question: Does the web load balancer (aws_lb.web) encode values it puts into HTTP headers?
questions.why: Header injection splits responses.

questions.question: Does traffic to HTTPS/443 (GRAPH-017) run over a VPN or private link?
questions.why: Private links reduce who can reach it.

questions.question: Does the app server (aws_instance.app) check sizes and ranges of input (lengths, counts, numbers)?
questions.why: Out-of-range input causes crashes and memory bugs.

questions.question: Does the app server (aws_instance.app) limit request sizes, rates and time per request?
questions.why: Without limits, one client can exhaust the service.

questions.question: Does the app server (aws_instance.app) use a standard authentication scheme (OIDC, SAML, signed tokens) rather than a home-made one?
questions.why: Home-made authentication is easy to get subtly wrong.

questions.question: Can the app server (aws_instance.app) keep working when a dependency fails (retries, fallbacks)?
questions.why: Cascading failures become outages.

questions.question: Does the app server (aws_instance.app) detect tampering with the data it handles (signatures, checksums)?
questions.why: Undetected tampering means you act on forged data.

questions.question: Does the app server (aws_instance.app) repeat validation on the server, not only in the browser?
questions.why: Browser checks are easily skipped.

questions.question: Is the code the app server (aws_instance.app) runs signed and checked before it runs?
questions.why: Unsigned code can be swapped.
